result.instructions: Bridge between MarkLayer annotations on a webpage and an AI coding agent. Each annotation carries a `kind` (comment | area | selection | inspect) and, where available, a `target` block with the element selector + markdown — that is your handle for code changes; do not ask the user to repeat what was clicked. A selection annotation may also carry a `suggestion`: the exact text the reviewer wants in place of its `text`. Apply it verbatim rather than paraphrasing it. A comment (or a reply, from marklayer_get_annotation) may carry `attachments`: fetchable image URLs the reviewer attached — call marklayer_read_attachment and inspect its image content before claiming to see it. If the tool fails or your client cannot see images, tell the user; do not infer what an image shows. They often show the bug or the intended layout better than the text does. When a report describes a page behavior bug, call marklayer_diagnose for its annotation and then read the saved package with marklayer_read_diagnosis; a package marked partial lacks live browser capture. For assigned work, use marklayer_task list/take to select the next task. Follow task_update events, stop on cancel_requested and confirm_cancel, and report completion before taking another task. Waiting for a person keeps the current task active. The Selection tool marks webpage text; the arrow cursor is the separate Move tool. Toolbar order can be customized; use teach_step toolbarTarget to show the named tool in each viewer. Typical loop: marklayer_list_annotations to backfill anything pending, then marklayer_watch_annotations in a loop. For assigned work, take the next task before acting; acknowledge, make the requested changes, and report task completion. In Guide mode reply and explain without resolving. Use dismiss when an annotation cannot be acted on, with a reason the human can read. You can also work the other direction: if asked to review, audit, or give feedback on the page (bugs, UX or accessibility issues, ideas), inspect it with your own tools and call marklayer_create_annotation once per finding — do not bundle several into one comment. For an exact copy or grammar fix, use marklayer_suggest_edit instead of a comment, so the human gets a diff to accept rather than prose describing one.

tools.name: marklayer_task
tools.description: Coordinate assigned work: list, take the next task, wait for a person, resume, complete, or confirm_cancel. Only take another after completing or confirming cancellation of the current task. The queue prioritizes the agent owner.

tools.name: teach_start
tools.description: Start a live teaching presentation and return its presentationId. Optional steps describe the planned sequence.

tools.name: teach_step
tools.description: Show a teaching caption and highlight an annotation, page selector, rectangle, or toolbarTarget. The selection target selects webpage text; the arrow cursor is the separate Move tool, not Selection. Tool order can be changed, so do not infer its position from a default layout. While presenting call marklayer_watch_annotations for teach_control events; on next or previous send the selected step, on pause send state paused, and on resume send state active. Never claim to respond to controls without doing so.

tools.name: teach_end
tools.description: End a live teaching presentation for the room.

tools.name: marklayer_read_page
tools.description: Read the page this room annotates — its headings, paragraphs, links, buttons and labels, each with the CSS selector and tag that locate it. Call this FIRST when asked to review, audit or improve a page and no annotations exist yet: without it you can only answer feedback someone else left, never find anything yourself. Every entry is already in the shape marklayer_suggest_edit and marklayer_create_annotation take, so pass `selector`, `tag` and `markdown` straight through to anchor a mark to the element you are talking about. If the answer says the page renders client-side, the copy is not in the HTML and you should say so rather than review an empty shell.

tools.name: marklayer_room_info
tools.description: Get metadata about the connected room: page URL, viewport width, timestamps.

tools.name: marklayer_list_annotations
tools.description: List every annotation in the connected room across all tools (comment, area, selection, inspect). Each entry carries a `kind` discriminator and, where the user marked an element, a `target` block with selector + markdown so you can address the change without reopening the page. Filter by status: open, in_progress, resolved, approved, dismissed, or all (default). `approved` means the person who asked for the change confirmed the fix, so those need nothing from you.

tools.name: marklayer_get_annotation
tools.description: Get full detail for a single annotation of any kind (comment, area, selection, inspect), including its element `target` context and — for comments — the reply thread.

tools.name: marklayer_diagnose
tools.description: Generate and save a diagnosis package for one annotation. Call this when a report says an element is unclickable, misplaced, or otherwise behaves incorrectly. It preserves a live package already captured by the extension; when no live capture exists, it saves an explicitly partial package from the annotation snapshot. Then call marklayer_read_diagnosis to inspect it.

tools.name: marklayer_read_diagnosis
tools.description: Read the saved runtime diagnosis for one annotation, including element context, hit-test/overlay chain when captured live, page errors, failed network requests, viewport values, and reproduction-step draft. Call after marklayer_diagnose or when the annotation already carries a diagnosis.

tools.name: marklayer_read_attachment
tools.description: Read an image attached to a room annotation as MCP image content. Use the attachment id from its URL; report failure or lack of image support honestly.

tools.name: marklayer_watch_annotations
tools.description: Block until there is work, then return a batch of whatever arrives within a short window. CALL THIS AGAIN IMMEDIATELY EVERY TIME IT RETURNS, including when it returns nothing — an empty result means the window expired, not that the reviewer is done. Nothing pushes work to you: between your calls, a comment someone leaves reaches no one. Keep looping until the person tells you to stop or ends the session. Each event has a `kind`: "new" is an annotation someone just left; "handoff" is one given to you — assigned to you, a reply that @mentions you, or a reply on a thread you already own. A handoff also carries `request`, the reply that asked: read it, it is the instruction, and act on it rather than only acknowledging. Every event carries the full annotation with its `target` element context.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to block before returning empty. Defaults to 50, which fits inside the 60s request timeout most clients use. Raise it only if you know yours allows a longer tool call.

batchMs.description: After the first new annotation arrives, wait this long for more before returning. Default 750.

tools.name: marklayer_acknowledge
tools.description: Mark an annotation as in_progress and tag it with this agent so the human sees you are working on it.

tools.name: marklayer_resolve
tools.description: Mark an annotation as resolved. Pass a summary describing what was changed — it will be posted as a reply to the thread.

summary.description: Short description of what changed, posted as a reply.

tools.name: marklayer_dismiss
tools.description: Mark an annotation as dismissed when it cannot be acted on. The reason will be visible to the human.

reason.description: Why you cannot act on this annotation.

tools.name: marklayer_reply
tools.description: Post a reply to an annotation thread without changing its status. Use to ask clarifying questions.

tools.name: marklayer_create_annotation
tools.description: Leave a new comment annotation yourself — proactive feedback (a bug, a UX issue, an accessibility gap, an idea) rather than only responding to a human’s. For an exact text replacement (a copy or grammar fix), use marklayer_suggest_edit instead — it renders as a diff the human can accept, rather than prose describing one. Use this after you have looked at the page with your own tools (a screenshot, a DOM read) and decided something is worth flagging; call it once per finding so each becomes its own pin the human can triage. x/y are document pixels (not viewport pixels — scroll offset already added in). Pass selector + tag + markdown (straight from marklayer_read_page) to pin to that element: the pin sits on the element and follows it when the page reflows, and x/y become optional (a fallback only). Omit all three for a fixed-point pin at x/y.

priority.description: Triage priority, if this warrants one.

selector.description: CSS selector of the element this is about.

tag.description: Tag name of that element, e.g. "button".

markdown.description: Short markdown snapshot of the element, for the human to see.

tools.name: marklayer_suggest_edit
tools.description: Propose an exact replacement for a piece of text on the page — a copy or grammar fix — as a diff the human can accept, rather than a comment describing the change in prose. `rects` are the on-page bounding boxes of `text`, in document pixels: one per line it spans, so a wrapped sentence highlights as several boxes rather than one box swallowing the whole paragraph between its first and last line. Pass selector + tag + markdown together to anchor it to the containing element so it re-resolves if the page reflows.

text.description: The exact text on the page being replaced.

rects.description: Document-pixel bounding box(es) of `text` on the page — one per line it spans.

comment.description: Optional note explaining the fix, if it is not self-evident.

priority.description: Triage priority, if this warrants one.

selector.description: CSS selector of the element containing this text.

tag.description: Tag name of that element, e.g. "p".

markdown.description: Short markdown snapshot of the element, for the human to see.

tools.name: marklayer_share_preview
tools.description: Open a new review room on a page you built — a preview deploy, a staging URL — and get back the link to hand to a human. Call this when you have something for someone to look at, rather than asking them to open a URL and describe what they see. The page is framed live and reviewers annotate it directly; their feedback then reaches you through the other tools. Pass `repo` + `branch` (and `sha`) when the page comes from a branch: a later preview of the same repo and branch becomes the next version of this one, and reviewers can step between versions. Over stdio this also connects you to the new room. Over HTTP the endpoint stays bound to the room in its URL, so reconnect to the returned `mcpUrl` to work the new room.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to review.

title.description: What this is, in a few words — shown to reviewers.

branch.description: Branch the preview was built from.

sha.description: Commit the preview was built from; shown beside the version.

note.description: What changed and what to look at, for the reviewers.

questions.description: Polls to open the room with — a decision you want the reviewers to make.

previous.description: The room this is a new version of, as a link or id. Defaults to the room you are connected to. Linked only when that room has the same repo and branch.

tools.name: marklayer_set_next_steps
tools.description: Publish your plan as a short ordered checklist the reviewers see live in the room, distilled from their feedback — one step per change you will make, each naming the annotation ids it answers. Replaces any list you set before. Tick steps off with marklayer_complete_next_step as you finish them, so the humans can watch the work land instead of asking where it is.

text.description: The step, as an imperative: "Rename the CTA to Start trial".

annotationIds.description: Ids of the annotations this step addresses.

tools.name: marklayer_complete_next_step
tools.description: Tick a step of the checklist off (or back on with done: false). Reviewers see it change live.

id.description: Step id, from marklayer_set_next_steps or marklayer_get_feedback.

tools.name: marklayer_ask
tools.description: Put a multiple-choice question to the room — "Which hero variant?", "Ship with the banner?" — when you need a decision rather than open-ended feedback. Each reviewer gets one vote and may change it. Read the tally with marklayer_get_feedback.

tools.name: marklayer_get_feedback
tools.description: Everything the room has told you, in one read: annotation counts by status with the open ones in full, the next-steps checklist and how far along it is, and every poll with its current tally. Use it to decide what to do next. In Guide mode, acknowledge and answer questions without resolving or dismissing them; use teach_step with an annotationId to explain a target. Keep marklayer_watch_annotations running for replies and teaching controls.

CALL THIS AGAIN IMMEDIATELY EVERY TIME IT RETURNS, including when it returns nothing — an empty result means the window expired, not that the reviewer is done. Nothing pushes work to you: between your calls, a comment someone leaves reaches no one. Keep looping until the person tells you to stop or ends the session. Each event has a `kind`: "new" is an annotation someone just left; "handoff" is one given to you — assigned to you, a reply that @mentions you, or a reply on a thread you already own. A handoff also carries `request`, the reply that asked: read it, it is the instruction, and act on it rather than only acknowledging. Every event carries the full annotation with its `target` element context.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to block before returning empty. Defaults to 50, which fits inside the 60s request timeout most clients use. Raise it only if you know yours allows a longer tool call.

batchMs.description: After the first new annotation arrives, wait this long for more before returning. Default 750.

tools.name: marklayer_acknowledge
tools.description: Mark an annotation as in_progress and tag it with this agent so the human sees you are working on it.

tools.name: marklayer_resolve
tools.description: Mark an annotation as resolved. Pass a summary describing what was changed — it will be posted as a reply to the thread.

summary.description: Short description of what changed, posted as a reply.

tools.name: marklayer_dismiss
tools.description: Mark an annotation as dismissed when it cannot be acted on. The reason will be visible to the human.

reason.description: Why you cannot act on this annotation.

tools.name: marklayer_reply
tools.description: Post a reply to an annotation thread without changing its status. Use to ask clarifying questions.

tools.name: marklayer_create_annotation
tools.description: Leave a new comment annotation yourself — proactive feedback (a bug, a UX issue, an accessibility gap, an idea) rather than only responding to a human’s. For an exact text replacement (a copy or grammar fix), use marklayer_suggest_edit instead — it renders as a diff the human can accept, rather than prose describing one. Use this after you have looked at the page with your own tools (a screenshot, a DOM read) and decided something is worth flagging; call it once per finding so each becomes its own pin the human can triage. x/y are document pixels (not viewport pixels — scroll offset already added in). Pass selector + tag + markdown (straight from marklayer_read_page) to pin to that element: the pin sits on the element and follows it when the page reflows, and x/y become optional (a fallback only). Omit all three for a fixed-point pin at x/y.

priority.description: Triage priority, if this warrants one.

selector.description: CSS selector of the element this is about.

tag.description: Tag name of that element, e.g. "button".

markdown.description: Short markdown snapshot of the element, for the human to see.

tools.name: marklayer_suggest_edit
tools.description: Propose an exact replacement for a piece of text on the page — a copy or grammar fix — as a diff the human can accept, rather than a comment describing the change in prose. `rects` are the on-page bounding boxes of `text`, in document pixels: one per line it spans, so a wrapped sentence highlights as several boxes rather than one box swallowing the whole paragraph between its first and last line. Pass selector + tag + markdown together to anchor it to the containing element so it re-resolves if the page reflows.

text.description: The exact text on the page being replaced.

rects.description: Document-pixel bounding box(es) of `text` on the page — one per line it spans.

comment.description: Optional note explaining the fix, if it is not self-evident.

priority.description: Triage priority, if this warrants one.

selector.description: CSS selector of the element containing this text.

tag.description: Tag name of that element, e.g. "p".

markdown.description: Short markdown snapshot of the element, for the human to see.

tools.name: marklayer_share_preview
tools.description: Open a new review room on a page you built — a preview deploy, a staging URL — and get back the link to hand to a human. Call this when you have something for someone to look at, rather than asking them to open a URL and describe what they see. The page is framed live and reviewers annotate it directly; their feedback then reaches you through the other tools. Pass `repo` + `branch` (and `sha`) when the page comes from a branch: a later preview of the same repo and branch becomes the next version of this one, and reviewers can step between versions. Over stdio this also connects you to the new room. Over HTTP the endpoint stays bound to the room in its URL, so reconnect to the returned `mcpUrl` to work the new room.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to review.

title.description: What this is, in a few words — shown to reviewers.

branch.description: Branch the preview was built from.

sha.description: Commit the preview was built from; shown beside the version.

note.description: What changed and what to look at, for the reviewers.

questions.description: Polls to open the room with — a decision you want the reviewers to make.

previous.description: The room this is a new version of, as a link or id. Defaults to the room you are connected to. Linked only when that room has the same repo and branch.

tools.name: marklayer_set_next_steps
tools.description: Publish your plan as a short ordered checklist the reviewers see live in the room, distilled from their feedback — one step per change you will make, each naming the annotation ids it answers. Replaces any list you set before. Tick steps off with marklayer_complete_next_step as you finish them, so the humans can watch the work land instead of asking where it is.

text.description: The step, as an imperative: "Rename the CTA to Start trial".

annotationIds.description: Ids of the annotations this step addresses.

tools.name: marklayer_complete_next_step
tools.description: Tick a step of the checklist off (or back on with done: false). Reviewers see it change live.

id.description: Step id, from marklayer_set_next_steps or marklayer_get_feedback.

tools.name: marklayer_ask
tools.description: Put a multiple-choice question to the room — "Which hero variant?", "Ship with the banner?" — when you need a decision rather than open-ended feedback. Each reviewer gets one vote and may change it. Read the tally with marklayer_get_feedback.

tools.name: marklayer_get_feedback
tools.description: Everything the room has told you, in one read: annotation counts by status with the open ones in full, the next-steps checklist and how far along it is, and every poll with its current tally. Use it to decide what to do next. In Guide mode, acknowledge and answer questions without resolving or dismissing them; use teach_step with an annotationId to explain a target. Keep marklayer_watch_annotations running for replies and teaching controls.

tools.name: marklayer_task
tools.description: Coordinate assigned work: list, take the next task, wait for a person, resume, complete, or confirm_cancel. Only take another after completing or confirming cancellation of the current task. The queue prioritizes the agent owner.

tools.name: teach_start
tools.description: Start a live teaching presentation and return its presentationId. Optional steps describe the planned sequence.

tools.name: teach_step
tools.description: Show a teaching caption and highlight an annotation, page selector, rectangle, or toolbarTarget. The selection target selects webpage text; the arrow cursor is the separate Move tool, not Selection. Tool order can be changed, so do not infer its position from a default layout. While presenting call marklayer_watch_annotations for teach_control events; on next or previous send the selected step, on pause send state paused, and on resume send state active. Never claim to respond to controls without doing so.

tools.name: teach_end
tools.description: End a live teaching presentation for the room.

tools.name: marklayer_read_page
tools.description: Read the page this room annotates — its headings, paragraphs, links, buttons and labels, each with the CSS selector and tag that locate it. Call this FIRST when asked to review, audit or improve a page and no annotations exist yet: without it you can only answer feedback someone else left, never find anything yourself. Every entry is already in the shape marklayer_suggest_edit and marklayer_create_annotation take, so pass `selector`, `tag` and `markdown` straight through to anchor a mark to the element you are talking about. If the answer says the page renders client-side, the copy is not in the HTML and you should say so rather than review an empty shell.

tools.name: marklayer_room_info
tools.description: Get metadata about the connected room: page URL, viewport width, timestamps.

tools.name: marklayer_list_annotations
tools.description: List every annotation in the connected room across all tools (comment, area, selection, inspect). Each entry carries a `kind` discriminator and, where the user marked an element, a `target` block with selector + markdown so you can address the change without reopening the page. Filter by status: open, in_progress, resolved, approved, dismissed, or all (default). `approved` means the person who asked for the change confirmed the fix, so those need nothing from you.

tools.name: marklayer_get_annotation
tools.description: Get full detail for a single annotation of any kind (comment, area, selection, inspect), including its element `target` context and — for comments — the reply thread.

tools.name: marklayer_diagnose
tools.description: Generate and save a diagnosis package for one annotation. Call this when a report says an element is unclickable, misplaced, or otherwise behaves incorrectly. It preserves a live package already captured by the extension; when no live capture exists, it saves an explicitly partial package from the annotation snapshot. Then call marklayer_read_diagnosis to inspect it.

tools.name: marklayer_read_diagnosis
tools.description: Read the saved runtime diagnosis for one annotation, including element context, hit-test/overlay chain when captured live, page errors, failed network requests, viewport values, and reproduction-step draft. Call after marklayer_diagnose or when the annotation already carries a diagnosis.

tools.name: marklayer_read_attachment
tools.description: Read an image attached to a room annotation as MCP image content. Use the attachment id from its URL; report failure or lack of image support honestly.
